question: Assume today is 2026-08-25. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate total U.S. net electricity generation at utility-scale facilities (all sectors, all energy sources, excluding small-scale solar) in July 2026, in gigawatt-hours (GWh, equal to thousand megawatthours), as it will be first reported in the U.S. Energy Information Administration's Electric Power Monthly (Table 1.1).

target.what: Total U.S. net electricity generation at utility-scale facilities, all sectors and all energy sources, excluding small-scale solar (EIA Electric Power Monthly Table 1.1 'Net Generation by Energy Source: Total (All Sectors)'), as first reported
target.publisher: U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA), Electric Power Monthly
target.cadence: Monthly, with preliminary figures first published roughly two months after the reference month (typically mid-to-late of the following month)
target.caveats: Target period is future relative to the 2026-08-25 cutoff, so no July 2026 data exist yet; must be forecast. 'Utility-scale' excludes small-scale solar (EIA-923/860 facilities); all sectors (electric power, industrial, commercial CHP) included. 'Net generation' is gross minus plant parasitic load. F

candidates.hypothesis: July 2026 total generation ≈ July 2025 total adjusted for year-over-year load growth and weather; July is typically the annual peak month. Prior July values and recent monthly values (through the latest published month before cutoff, likely May or June 2026) anchor the level and trend.
candidates.data_to_find: EIA Table 1.1 total net generation (all sectors, all sources) for July 2023, July 2024, July 2025, and the most recent published months (Jan–Jun 2026 if available). Also year-over-year growth rates in recent months.

kept.applies_when: July 2026 weather-driven demand is at least as high as July 2025 and the 1H26 growth trend persists into July.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that July 2026 CDD was below July 2025, or that 2026 generation growth stalled or reversed.

kept.name: All-sectors utility-scale total as a multiple of the electric-power-sector total
kept.rationale: EIA Table 7d reports the electric-power-sector total; the all-sectors total adds industrial and commercial CHP, which historically runs roughly 4-6% of the electric-power-sector total. A 1.05 multiple with a 1.02-1.09 range reflects that CHP margin and revision uncertainty.
kept.applies_when: The all-sectors total exceeds the electric-power-sector total by a modest CHP margin.
kept.falsified_by: An EIA all-sectors July 2025 total materially outside 1.02-1.09 times the electric-power-sector total.

kept.name: Months per quarter (calendar constant as named input)
kept.rationale: A quarter contains three months; used to convert the 3Q25 quarterly total (p54) to a monthly average. This is a fixed calendar constant, not an empirical estimate.
kept.applies_when: Converting a quarterly total to a monthly average.
kept.falsified_by: Nothing; it is a definitional calendar constant.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
